General anesthesia with femoral nerve block for peri-operative analgesia
General anesthesia for cholecystectomy in 2009; no complications reported

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: Good morning, Mr./Ms. [Name]. I'm [Provider's Name], the anesthesiologist who'll be taking care of you during your knee surgery tomorrow. Let's go over some details to ensure everything is in order. How have you been feeling lately?

segments.speaker: PATIENT
segments.text: Morning, doc. Been managing okay lah, but this left knee is really giving me trouble. Can't walk far without pain, even with the brace.

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: I see. How long have you been experiencing these symptoms, and has there been any recent worsening?

segments.speaker: PATIENT
segments.text: About 2 years now, but last 6 months it's gotten much worse. Can't even climb stairs properly, you know?

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: Understood. Let's move to your medications. I see you're on Metformin, Amlodipine, Metoprolol, Atorvastatin, and Lisinopril. Are all these still active, or have there been any changes recently?

segments.speaker: PATIENT
segments.text: Ah, actually, doc. I stopped Lisinopril about 6 months ago. Had a bad dry cough from it, couldn't sleep. Doctor said to stop and switch to something else, but I think the records might still show it as active?

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: Thank you for clarifying that. So, to confirm: you're no longer on Lisinopril, and your current active medications are Metformin, Amlodipine, Metoprolol, and Atorvastatin?

segments.speaker: PATIENT
segments.text: Yes, that's right. The cough went away after stopping Lisinopril, and the other meds are all still going strong.

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: Excellent, that's important to note. Any known allergies to medications or other substances?

segments.speaker: PATIENT
segments.text: None that I know of, doc. Never had a reaction to anything.

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: Great. Have you had anything to eat or drink since midnight? We need to confirm your NPO status.

segments.speaker: PATIENT
segments.text: Nope, nothing since 12am. Just a sip of water for meds this morning, like you instructed.

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: Perfect. Have you had any prior surgeries or anesthesia? Any complications in the past?

segments.speaker: PATIENT
segments.text: Had a hernia surgery years back. Anesthesia was fine then, no issues. Woke up feeling okay lah.

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: Good to hear. Lastly, how would you describe your overall fitness? Can you walk with assistance, climb stairs, or do you need a wheelchair?

segments.speaker: PATIENT
segments.text: With the knee brace and a walking stick, I can manage short distances. But without it, it's really painful. Can't do stairs at all now.

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: Thank you for sharing that. We'll plan for general anesthesia with a femoral nerve block to manage your pain during and after surgery. Your blood pressure medications will continue as usual, and we'll monitor your diabetes closely. Any questions for me?

segments.speaker: PATIENT
segments.text: No questions, doc. Just want to get this sorted so I can walk properly again. Thanks for listening.

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: Of course, Mr./Ms. [Name]. We'll take good care of you. I'll see you in the pre-op area tomorrow. Rest well tonight.

segments.speaker: PATIENT
segments.text: Will do, doc. Appreciate it.

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: [08:00] induction propofol one hundred twenty milligrams

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: [08:05] tube in, grade one view

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: [08:10] right radial artery line placed

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: [08:15] one thousand milliliters of lactated ringers administered

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: [08:25] mean arterial pressure dropped to fifty, treated with one hundred and fifty micrograms of phenylephrine

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: [08:35] heart rate increased to one hundred ten, treated with twenty milligrams of labetalol

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: [08:45] left femoral nerve block performed with twenty milliliters of ropivacaine

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: Mr Tan, how are you feeling now after the surgery?

segments.speaker: PATIENT
segments.text: I have some pain at the knee, but it's manageable. Not too bad, doc.

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: On a scale of 1 to 10, how would you rate the pain?

segments.speaker: PATIENT
segments.text: Maybe 4? The numbness from the block is still there, so it's not too painful.

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: Any nausea or vomiting since waking up?

segments.speaker: PATIENT
segments.text: A bit queasy earlier, but better now. Didn't throw up, though.

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: How's your breathing? Any discomfort in your chest or throat?

segments.speaker: PATIENT
segments.text: Slight sore throat from the tube, but I can breathe fine.

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: Do you remember anything from the operation?

segments.speaker: PATIENT
segments.text: No, everything's a blank. Woke up here, so that's good.

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: Any issues with your blood pressure or sugar levels that you're aware of?

segments.speaker: PATIENT
segments.text: My sugar was a bit high before surgery, but the nurses said they're monitoring it. BP seems okay now.
